Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 64, verses 5–6:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the earlier nations and what punishment and retribution befell them for opposing the messengers and denying the truth. He says: ﴿Has there not come to you the news of those who disbelieved before?﴾ That is: inform them of what their affair was. ﴿So they tasted the bad consequence of their conduct﴾ That is: the evil outcome of their denial and the wretchedness of their deeds, which is what befell them in this world of punishment and disgrace. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ That is: in the Hereafter, in addition to this worldly punishment.

Then He gave the reason for that, saying: ﴿That is because there came to them their messengers with clear proofs﴾ That is: with arguments, evidences and demonstrations. ﴿So they said, "Will mere humans guide us?"﴾ That is: they considered it improbable that messengers should be human, and that their guidance should come through the hands of humans like themselves. ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away﴾ That is: they denied the truth and shrank back from acting upon it. ﴿But Allah is free of need﴾ That is: of them. ﴿And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 64, verses 7–10:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the polytheists, the disbelievers, and the atheists, that they claim they will not be resurrected: ﴿Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did."﴾ That is, you will surely be informed of all your deeds, the great and the trivial, the small and the large. ﴿And that is easy for Allah.﴾ That is, your resurrection and your recompense.

This is the third verse in which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to swear by his Lord, exalted and majestic, to the occurrence and reality of the return (al-ma'ad). The first is in Surah Yunus: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is surely true, and you cannot escape it."﴾ [Yunus: 53]. The second is in Surah Saba': ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾ [Saba': 3], and the verse continues. The third is this one: [﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did, and that is easy for Allah."﴾] [[An addition from manuscript M, section 1.]]

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the light which We have sent down.﴾ That is, the Qur'an. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ That is, nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾, this is the Day of Resurrection. It is called that because the first and the last will be gathered on one level plain (sa'id), the caller will make them hear, and the sight will penetrate them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud: 103], and He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 49–50].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss (taghabun)﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, because the people of Paradise will cheat the people of the Fire. Qatadah and Mujahid said the same.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: there is no greater loss than that these (the people of Paradise) are admitted to Paradise while those (the people of the Fire) are taken to the Fire.

I say: This has been explained by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein forever; and wretched is the destination.﴾ The explanation of similar passages has already preceded more than once.

﴿No calamity strikes except by the permission of Allah.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: "By the command of Allah, meaning by His decree and His will." [[In A: "by His power."]]

﴿And whoever believes in Allah – He will guide his heart. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ That is: whoever is struck by a calamity and knows that it is by the decree and destiny of Allah, and is patient, seeks reward, and submits to the decree of Allah, Allah will guide his heart and will compensate him for what he lost of worldly things with guidance in his heart and true certainty. As for His saying: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful﴾, its explanation has preceded in Surat al-Hashr, along with the hadiths related to the meaning of this verse, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you﴾, meaning: whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and whatever you give in charity, its reward is with Him. This is treated as a loan to Him, as established in the Sahih that Allah, the Exalted, says: "Whoever lends to one who is neither unjust nor poor" [Sahih Muslim no. (758), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him]. Therefore He said: ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾, as was mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And He will multiply it for him many times over﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

﴿And forgive you﴾, meaning: He will expiate your misdeeds. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is Appreciative﴾, meaning He rewards a little with much, ﴿Forbearing﴾, meaning [He pardons,] forgives, conceals, and overlooks the sins, lapses, errors, and misdeeds.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the Wise﴾ Its explanation has been mentioned more than once.
